pilot_batch_target_images: 50-100 real smartphone photos legally captured by project team
scene_and_context_checklist: Household open trash bin / kitchen waste corner (concrete, tile, wet courtyard)
Residential alley collection point / street-side bin apron (asphalt, brick, sidewalk)
Student dormitory / campus recycling drop-off point
Outdoor park soil / grass / rain gutter / curb-side litter context
Garage / e-waste collection box / workbench with discarded batteries and mixed packaging

per_class_object_checklist.3_clothes: Torn shirts, stained rags, discarded single gloves, old socks, worn fabric scraps, wet/soiled garments.
per_class_object_checklist.8_shoes: Broken flip-flops, single abandoned sneakers, worn-out sandals, detached soles, muddy boots.
per_class_object_checklist.0_battery: Spent AA/AAA/9V/C/D alkaline cells, corroded batteries, swollen Li-ion pouches, coin cells, old UPS/motorbike lead-acid batteries.
per_class_object_checklist.4_glass: Empty glass beverage/sauce bottles, cosmetic glass jars, intact or safely boxed broken glass fragments in bins.
per_class_object_checklist.1_biological: Fruit peels (banana, orange, mango), vegetable trimmings, eggshells, spoiled bread/rice, wilted leaves/food scraps.

single_multi_object_multiclass_protocol.single_object_ratio: 30% of shots (1 target scarce-class item on realistic waste background)
single_multi_object_multiclass_protocol.multi_object_same_class_ratio: 25% of shots (2-5 distinct items of the same scarce class, e.g., 3 spent batteries or 2 old shoes)
single_multi_object_multiclass_protocol.multiclass_co_occurrence_ratio: 45% of shots (target scarce item placed alongside 1-3 other waste classes such as plastic wrapper, metal can, paper, or organic peel)

specimen_and_session_id_rules.independence_rule: Up to 3 angles per physical specimen are permitted to support training, but all angles share the SAME specimen_id, count as 1 unique specimen, and are locked to the same split (never split across train and val).

ten_class_full_annotation_guide.rule_1_annotate_every_visible_waste_item: Every visible waste object in the frame belonging to ANY of the 10 canonical classes (0..9) MUST be annotated with its own tight bounding box.
ten_class_full_annotation_guide.rule_2_no_merged_boxes: Never draw one group box over multiple adjacent items unless physically fused into an inseparable single mass.
ten_class_full_annotation_guide.rule_3_occlusion_handling: Annotate partially occluded waste items if >= 25% of the item is visible and material identity is unambiguous.
